passages.text: Try this prompt with your AI tool of choice:

`You are my most perceptive ally. Read everything I have written in our conversations so far. Identify where my words suggest self-doubt or imposter feelings, even if I have not named them directly. Reflect on what story I might be telling myself about my abilities. Offer one alternative interpretation that highlights real evidence of skill, progress, or value. Then suggest one small confidence-building action I can take to act from that stronger perspective. Return your response in three parts: Reframe (a new interpretation of the story), Proof (specific evidence that supports it), and Step (a simple action that embodies self-trust).`
From what the AI returns, choose one action to act on immediately.
If you choose a Reframe, say the new statement aloud until it feels true.
If you choose a Proof, note it down and keep it visible while you work.
If you choose a Step, do it, even if it feels small or slightly uncomfortable.
The aim is not to erase doubt but to retrain how you read it. Each response is a quiet act of rebalancing: turning uncertainty into data and reclaiming the right to trust your own competence.
If you are new to *Slow AI*, here is our first invitation.
#### Slow AI #1 – Teach It Something It Cannot Know

That’s when I ran the AI prompt. Instead of asking for reassurance, I asked it to reflect back on my strengths. The response reminded me: I wasn’t proving anything; I was refining insight, shaping words, and claiming authorship. Reading the lines aloud, seeing evidence of skill I’d overlooked, gave me a small but powerful jolt of confidence.
